name: Steven Hoffenberg

summary.text: Steven J. Hoffenberg (1945-2022) ran Towers Financial Corporation, a New York debt-collection and factoring company. The SEC sued him in February 1993; he pleaded guilty in April 1995 to conspiring to commit securities fraud and was sentenced in March 1997 to 20 years in prison, a $1 million fine and about $475 million in restitution. He was released from federal custody in 2013. After his release he filed suits in 2016 and 2018 asserting that Jeffrey Epstein, whom he had hired as a consultant in the late 1980s, had designed the Towers fraud; both suits were withdrawn and Epstein was never charged. Hoffenberg was found dead in Derby, Connecticut in August 2022 at age 77.

facts.claim: The SEC sued Hoffenberg, Towers Financial and two other executives on February 8, 1993, alleging an unregistered offering of promissory notes and misrepresentations about Towers' financial condition; it also charged him with selling Towers stock while possessing inside information that it was worthless.
facts.quote: The SEC also charged Hoffenberg with failing to register the offerings of promissory notes with the SEC, and selling his Towers common stock while in possession of inside information that the stock was worthless.

facts.claim: Hoffenberg pleaded guilty on April 20, 1995 to conspiring to commit securities fraud under Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5, admitting he knew Towers' financial statements overstated its assets and revenues and that he made entries in Towers' books he knew were false.
facts.quote: He also described making entries in Towers' books that he knew were false, in furtherance of the conspiracy.

facts.claim: On March 7, 1997 Judge Robert W. Sweet sentenced Hoffenberg to twenty years' imprisonment, three years' supervised release, a $1 million fine and approximately $475 million in restitution; a 2011 Third Circuit order described the sentence as following his guilty plea to conspiracy to violate the securities laws and other offenses.
facts.quote: Hoffenberg is presently confined at FCI-Fort Dix in New Jersey, where he is serving a twenty-year sentence imposed by the District Court for the Southern District of New York in 1997 following his plea of guilty to conspiracy to violate the securities laws and other offenses.

facts.claim: Hoffenberg hired Jeffrey Epstein as a consultant to Towers from about 1987, paying him $25,000 a month and extending a $2 million loan in 1988, according to CBS News.
facts.quote: Hoffenberg hired Epstein from about 1987 to 1993 to help with the Towers Financial Corporation, paid him $25,000 a month and gave him a $2 million loan in 1988 that Epstein would never have to pay back.

facts.claim: In 2016 Hoffenberg sued Epstein seeking a 'constructive trust' over Epstein's businesses for the benefit of Towers victims; Epstein's lawyers argued the claims were time-barred, that Epstein's firm was formed years after the scheme, and that Hoffenberg lacked standing. Both the 2016 suit and a 2018 investors' suit were withdrawn.
